newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs eye U.S. data amid nerves over rates.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs eye U.S. data amid nerves over rates.

text.p: Belgian capital market rates held basically steady on Monday, with little fresh news emerging to steer prices, putting the focus firmly on data due this week from the other side of the Atlantic, dealers said.

The outlook centres on fourth quarter U.S. employment cost data due on Tuesday. The figures were recently yanked into the limelight by senior U.S. Fed representatives. The market expects to glean clues as to U.S. interest rate policy from them.
Dealers said that if the headline number exceeded the average forecast of 1.2 percent, double the 0.6 percent seen in the third quarter, bond prices would be knocked down.

Dealers said it was not set in stone that higher U.S. rates meant instant increases in European rates, but a U.S. rate rise would remind investors that the bottom of the European cycle had either been reached or was not far away and that a move-up would be the next step for European rates.
The day's two key news items, although worrying, mainly reinforced ongoing issues, they said.

The arrest of two officials from one of the parties in the ruling Belgian coalition in connection with a bribery scandal sparked some talk of a government collapse, but traders said the scandal would have to deepen for that to happen.

There was no notable impact on bond prices. But the Belgian franc eased slightly against the mark to 20.6180/10 from 20.6170/80 late on Friday, even though it was off the day's low at 20.6215. The wider gap between bid/ask pointed to some market nervousness over the scandal, dealers said.
The other headline attracting attention was the cancellation of Boris Yeltsin's planned trip to the Netherlands to meet Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok on February 4.
Here too there was no clear impact with dealers saying the Russian president had been ailing for quite a while. He is recovering from double pneumonia.
Frontmonth OLO futures slipped with German Bund futures, breaking below 121.40, but support at 121.32 held. The future closed down 0.03 at 121.39.

In the cash market the benchmark 2007 OLO yielded 5.85 percent at the close, down one basis point from Friday's 5.84 percent. The issue's yield premium over similar Bunds narrowed to five bps from seven on Friday, but dealers said there was too little direction in the market for the recent five to seven bps range to be broken.
